prompt_history.name: stone_sizes_depletion_v1
prompt_history.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Edit/expand the supplied original game boulder into a polished landscape CONCEPT APPROVAL SHEET, not a runtime atlas. Keep the exact established pale granite identity, warm cream-grey angular faces, restrained dark outlines and soft dimensional cartoon fantasy rendering. Same fixed orthographic isometric camera, about35 degree downward elevation, same light from upper left. Clean warm off-white sheet, no black halo, no UI, no scenery, no photorealism.
Top half: three clearly separate harvestable rock forms at ONE COMMON WORLD SCALE on the same baseline: small (the supplied original rock silhouette), medium (substantially larger irregular boulder group), large (a substantial outcrop, still an individual hand-mined rock, never a stepped industrial quarry). Clearly increasing physical volume and varied natural silhouettes, not three scaled identical images. Short Russian labels only: "МАЛЫЙ", "СРЕДНИЙ", "БОЛЬШОЙ".
Bottom half: four ordered depletion KEY STATES of the SAME medium boulder, all at the same scale and registered ground anchor: intact, visibly chipped aboutone quarter removed, half extracted, small remaining core with most mass removed. Show physically removed chunks and reduced rock mass, not just uniform shrinking, tint/fade or growing cracks on an unchanged silhouette. Same rock identity and ground contact across states. Labels "100%", "75%", "50%", "15%". Do not add pickups, numbers for yields, tool icons, characters, buildings or industry. Generous gutters, all objects fully inside image, readable large forms rather than microtexture. This image is a review concept only; preserve the original source file and invent no mechanics.

prompt_history.name: hero_motion_keyposes_v1
prompt_history.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Transform the supplied original Hero C reference into a professional landscape ANIMATION KEYPOSE REVIEW SHEET, not a finished sprite atlas. Keep this exact man, face, tied dark hair, beard, blue embroidered travel tunic/scarf, cream sleeves, leather equipment/boots and olive trousers, modest backpack. Do not change outfit or character style. Same fixed orthographic elevated35-degree isometric camera, three-quarter screen-right facing for EVERY pose, same upper-left lighting and same physical body scale.
Three horizontal rows of SIX large fully visible keyposes, clear even gutters, warm off-white background. All six figures in each row share a planted-foot baseline and stable root location. Row1 "ХОДЬБА": a coherent full walking stride sequence with alternating left/right foot contact, down, passing, up, opposite contact and recovery; natural weight transfer, coordinated opposite arm swing, feet not skating. Hands free, bow absent for motion clarity. Row2 "КИРКА": a complete plausible TWO-HANDED pickaxe work sequence: ready, backswing, raised anticipation, downward strike, actual contact with one small stationary grey rock, recovery to ready. Same tool in every frame, hands gripping the handle, no extra arms, no weapon/tool morph. Row3 "ТОПОР": matching coherent chopping sequence: ready, backswing, anticipation, forward/down strike into a small stationary visible tree trunk, follow-through, recovery. Same practical wood/steel axe all6frames, fixed grip/anatomy and trunk location.
Poses must DIFFER meaningfully and connect physically; stable head size, torso/limb lengths, costume and foot anchor. Natural motion within the established cartoon style, no photorealism, no magic trails, exaggerated squash or motion-blur substitution. Label rows only with the three Russian titles above; no invented stats/UI. This is a storyboard of key poses for owner approval, not proof of smooth final animation and not runtime-ready art.

prompt_history.name: hero_motion_keyposes_v2
prompt_history.prompt:
Correct ONLY the top "ХОДЬБА" row of this concept sheet. Preserve the two lower "КИРКА"/"ТОПОР" rows, their complete characters/props/poses, labels, rendering and positions. Preserve exact Hero C identity/outfit/lighting/camera and all three-row layout. The walking row currently repeats wide-stride poses, so replace those6walking figures with six clearly DISTINCT keyposes of a single coherent full walk at the SAME three-quarter screen-right direction and common scale/ground baseline.
Pose1 CONTACT: feet widely split front/back, forward leg straight, rear heel raised, opposite arms counter-swing.
Pose2 DOWN: front foot planted under weight, front knee visibly flexed, hips slightly lower, rear toe lifting.
Pose3 PASSING: legs NARROW below torso, support leg near vertical, opposite knee BENT forward with raised foot beside support ankle, arms pass torso.
Pose4 OPPOSITE CONTACT: opposite leg now extended forward, feet widely split, opposite arm counter-swing (do not horizontally flip the character or change view).
Pose5 OPPOSITE DOWN: opposite weight-bearing knee flexed, modest lower hips, other toe lifting.
Pose6 OPPOSITE PASSING: feet/legs again NARROW under body, other knee bent forward, support leg vertical.
Strong visible difference between contact(WIDE), down(FLEXED), passing(NARROW) silhouettes. Do not show all six poses with the same leg extended. Feet may move within each cell; stable pelvis/root and constant limb lengths. No bow or new outfit, no extra arms, no turn toward camera, no floating. Keypose review only, not finished smooth animation.

prompt_history.name: skeleton_walk_keyposes_v2
prompt_history.prompt:
Rebuild this skeleton WALK KEYPOSE CONCEPT sheet because the current poses repeat the same wide split and frame8 changes view. Keep exact accepted character: ivory bones, red eyes/dark sockets, rounded skull, ragged dark-teal tunic, brown belt/brass buckle, no weapon. Same soft cartoon rendering, fixed three-quarter SCREEN-RIGHT view for EVERY frame,35degree elevated orthographic camera, same lighting and root scale, warm off-white backdrop.
Use EIGHT LARGE CLEARLY DIFFERENT keyposes, two rows of four, labels1–8. They are one continuous full gait cycle:
1 contact: feet WIDELY SPLIT front/back, near leg forward, far leg back, opposing arm swing.
2 down: near foot planted, near knee FLEXED, pelvis slightly lower, far heel rises.
3 passing: legs NARROW under hips, near supporting leg almost vertical, far knee BENT FORWARD with its raised foot passing beside support ankle; arms near torso.
4 up: near supporting heel lifts, far knee extends forward, pelvis slightly higher, feet still relatively close.
5 opposite contact: FAR leg forward, NEAR leg back, feet WIDELY SPLIT, opposite arm swing.
6 opposite down: far knee visibly flexed bearing weight, near foot lifts.
7 opposite passing: far support leg vertical under hips, near knee BENT FORWARD and raised foot passes beside support ankle, legs NARROW.
8 opposite up: far heel lifts and near leg prepares next forward contact.
Ensure CONTACT and PASSING silhouettes visibly differ (wide split versus narrow/one bent leg). Do not recycle the same extended legs for all poses. Same facing, skull and limb/bone lengths in all eight; distinguish near/far limbs naturally with lighting and overlap, not colored bands. No back-facing frame, jumps, rubber bones, extra limbs, background scene or motion blur. Large gutters, all toes fully visible. Concept keyposes for approval, NOT a finished animation atlas.
